title: Parity lifts and bounded-treewidth witnesses for Weisfeiler–Leman equivalence
main_claim: For k>=4 and t=k+1 (joint) or t=k (separate), a choice system on t domains yields uncolored graphs X_0, X_* of order at most A*M_t. They are k-WL equivalent iff the system has no successful choice, and a successful choice is detected after 2 joint rounds or 1 separate round. Under positive-rate ETH this gives an n^{Omega(k)} lower bound for fixed k; a uniform f(k)n^{o(k)} version follows under the weaker 2^{o(N)} hypothesis.
coverage:
Read all of the LaTeX (Sections 1–5) and checked each step by hand. Nothing needed a computer check.
- Lemma 2.1 (equal hom counts imply WL equivalence): the gluing invariant for rooted counts, the joint central bag of size k+1, the separate O/R bags of size k (including when y is identified with some u_j), the interpolation step, and the pure-tuple factorization for the disjoint union.
- Lemma 2.2 (detection): the formula for E_X; every triple lies in some k-face because k>=4; the separate-round formula for q_B; the case where y falls outside X_j in the disjoint union.
- Lemma 3.1 (lift duality): the solution set is the kernel or a translate of it, so differences never cancel; the F_2 Farkas argument; type masses equal 1 because T is connected.
- Lemma 3.2 (choice gives a witness).
- Lemma 4.1 (extraction): separators after contraction have size <=t-1, so the orientation is well defined; a sink exists and its outer sides partition V(F) minus B; B has exactly one vertex of each main type. Then P(V(F))=1 but P(B)=0. Each outer side contributes 0 in all cases: ell=i, ell=j, and ell outside {i,j} via helper h_{ij;ell}, the zero boundary correction and m_h=m_ell.
- Order bound M_t, Lemma 5.2 (SAT encoding), and the ETH rate arithmetic: eps<delta/4; B0C/t and 6qC/t below delta/4; 3Cqck/t<=delta/8; 2^{6ceil(m/t)}<=64*2^{6CN/t}.
- The racing/doubling cost bound in the uniform proposition, checked at a lighter level.
sibling_notes: The rank-259 companion paper (Unconditional time lower bounds) was reported no_gap_found. This paper says it does not use the companion's theorem, and I found no circular dependence between them.
